@Harry Hi Harry, thanks for the clean summary. One correction on item 1, and the rest are confirmed for you to proceed.

#### 1. AUTH_STARTED_AT column — keeping it (CTO direction)

After internal discussion (with CTO Justin), we'd like to keep the column.

* It's true that PG_CALLED_AT and AUTH_STARTED_AT happen at close moments in both OnePay and NicePay today, so they don't separate meaningfully right now.
* However, future PG integration changes or new PG integrations may introduce a separately-measurable authentication stage, and the migration cost of re-adding a dropped column would be high.
* So please keep both columns defined and have them store the same (or similar) value via INSERT/UPDATE for now.

#### 5. View + cross-DB owned by dev team ✅ Confirmed

BS_VENDOR_TRANSACTION_LOG mirror table creation + V_PAYMENT_FUNNEL 3-table view creation/maintenance both owned by dev team end-to-end.

author: Joseph
text:
# Runbook Update — Pilot Scope Amendment (v2)

Status: Scope decision · Owner: Joseph · Phase: C1 Foundation

Amends: the runbook draft above (v1). The §1 inventory and all technical procedures below remain valid — this amendment only narrows what gets executed during the pilot.

> Decision: In the pilot phase we execute §2 Move procedure ONLY (change the key SOURCE — read the same key bytes from Secrets Manager instead of the YAML literal). §3 Re-encryption (rotation) is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE for the pilot and is deferred to a later, dedicated document.

---

## 1. What the pilot WILL do — §2 Move only

* For api.kmsKey (and the two vendor keys as a coordinated value-swap where applicable), move the key value verbatim into Secrets Manager at omh/<env>/<service>/<key-name>, encrypted with alias/omh-secrets-<env>.
* The KMSKEY bind param value stays byte-for-byte identical → all existing ciphertext still decrypts → NO data migration, NO re-encryption.
* Validate per §4 (canary decrypt + count parity) in Dev → Staging.
* Rollback = config-only (revert to YAML literal), instant and safe — no data is ever touched.

## 2. What the pilot will NOT do — §3 deferred

* §3 (dual-key window + batch re-encrypt OLD→NEW) is NOT performed in the pilot.
* Rationale: re-encrypting data that is already encrypted at rest (38 columns / 17 tables incl. PM_PAYMENT_INFO card data) is a high-risk, irreversible-in-place operation. The §3 batch step is flagged in v1 as "the highest-risk step" — re-running OLD→NEW on an already-NEW row silently corrupts it.
* We will not take that risk until the entire secret-migration effort across all phases is complete and stable.

## 3. When §3 (re-encryption / rotation) will be reconsidered

* Only AFTER all phases of the secret migration are finished and the §2 Move is proven stable in production.
* The go/no-go on §3 will be decided in a separate follow-up document (not this runbook), which must re-confirm: the open items below, a maintenance/freeze window, and an idempotent + resumable migration job with a migrated-PK ledger.
* Until that document is approved, no key value is rotated — the pilot keeps the existing key value, just sourced from the vault.

## 4. Prerequisite still carried into the pilot

* Anomaly 1 (hardcoded api.kmsKey literal in PushHotelContentService.java:157 + SESTest.java) is a secret-leak issue independent of re-encryption and should still be tracked. Note: because the pilot keeps the same key value, this literal will not break decryption during the Move — but it remains a C-B3 secret-in-git-history leak and must be cleaned up before any future §3 rotation.

---

### Updated Definition of Done (pilot)

* §2 Move procedure reviewed by Security + a backend owner.
* §2 validated in Dev → Staging (canary decrypt passes, count parity holds).
* §3 Re-encryption explicitly marked DEFERRED — to be evaluated in a separate document post-migration.
* This amendment referenced from ELS-2051 (pilot) and ELS-2066 (move api.kmsKey). ELS-2073 (rotate) is gated behind the future §3 decision document.

author: Joseph
text:
# ⏸ DEFERRED — out of scope for the pilot

Per ELS-2049 runbook → Pilot Scope Amendment (v2). This ticket executes §3 Re-encryption (rotation) of the runbook, which is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE for the pilot and must NOT be started yet.

## Why this is blocked

* ELS-2073 rotates the actual key values for all three keys (C-B3 api.kmsKey, C-B4 hana AES key/iv, C-B5 abacus pcc-enc) → requires re-encrypting data at rest.
* For api.kmsKey that means re-encrypting 38 columns / 17 tables (incl. PM_PAYMENT_INFO card data) in a dual-key window — flagged in the runbook as "the highest-risk step" (re-running OLD→NEW on an already-NEW row silently corrupts it).
* Re-encrypting already-encrypted production data is a high-risk, hard-to-reverse operation; we will not take that risk until the secret-migration effort is otherwise complete and stable.

## Gate / preconditions before this can move

1. All phases of the secret migration are finished and the §2 Move (ELS-2066) is proven stable in production.
2. A separate §3 decision document is written and approved (NOT this runbook), re-confirming the runbook's open items:

   - MySQL AES_ENCRYPT mode in use (default AES-128-ECB) and any column on a different cipher.

   - Option A (batch re-encrypt) vs Option B (app-level dual-decrypt).

   - Whether writes can be frozen/redirected during the batch migration.

   - NEW key format/length constraints.

1. Anomaly 1 cleanup done first: strip the hardcoded api.kmsKey literal (PushHotelContentService.java:157, SESTest.java) and move it to @Value("${api.kmsKey}") — otherwise this path silently breaks (encrypt/decrypt with the dead key) after rotation. Blocker for cutover.
2. Idempotent + resumable migration job with a migrated-PK ledger (guard against double-encrypt corruption).

## Status

* Linked is blocked by ELS-2049.
* Keep in To Do / Deferred — do not pick up until the §3 decision document is approved.
* Vendor note: hana / abacus are in-flight keys (value-swap, no stored ciphertext); abacus pcc-enc NEW value must be re-issued by Abacus/Sabre, not generated by us.
